newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia sets 13.5 pct weighted public pay hike.
newsitem.headline: Colombia sets 13.5 pct weighted public pay hike.

text.p: Colombian Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo announced Thursday the pay increase, effective from January 1, for public sector employees would be a weighted 13.5 percent.

President Ernesto Samper's government is battling to rein in inflation and public spending after inflation hit 21.63 percent in 1996 and the government deficit reached four percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
The pay deal will save the government 300 billion pesos in 1997, Ocampo said at a news conference.

Those state employees who earn the equivalent of the minimum wage, currently about $142, will receive a 21 percent pay rise. Those who earn two minimum salaries will receive an 18 percent hike. For those public sector workers earning between two and three minimum salaries, the rise will be 14 percent, while those earning between three and four minimum wages will get a 10 percent hike.

The lowest increases will be for those public sector workers, including government ministers and the president, who earn in excess of four minimum wages -- their rise will amount to just eight percent.
"This a painful decision but the weighted increase will prevent the harshest effects falling on those with the lowest incomes," Ocampo said.
About 40 percent of state sector workers earn the minimum wage.
